beats.say: The data centre lease ends in March.
400 terabytes of history have to move to Google Cloud.
Plus MySQL, SQL Server and a Hadoop cluster. And not one row can go missing.
beats.label: Also moving
beats.head: Not one row can go missing

beats.say: Two ideas: how to move the bytes, and how to plan the move.
beats.label: Station 1.4 · Data migrations
beats.head: Move the bytes. Plan the move.

check.prompt: The copy would take months on your network line. What do you pick?
check.why: When the network needs more than about a week, ship a Transfer Appliance.

beats.say: Before you pick a tool, do the maths.
One terabyte over a 100 megabit line takes about 1 day.
beats.sub: per terabyte, on a 100 Mbps line

beats.say: So 400 terabytes would take more than a year. That is no good.
beats.label: On that line
beats.head: 400 TB = more than a year

beats.say: The rule: if the network needs more than about a week, ship a device.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: More than a week? Ship a device.

check.prompt: You must copy every MySQL change into BigQuery, all day. Which tool?
check.why: Datastream is serverless change data capture into BigQuery.

beats.say: Now match the job to the tool.
Huge data and a slow line? Transfer Appliance. Google ships you a box.
beats.label: Huge data, slow network
beats.head: Transfer Appliance
beats.text: A physical box, shipped to Google

beats.say: Big or repeating file copies, from S3 or on-prem? Storage Transfer Service.
beats.label: Files, big or recurring
beats.head: Storage Transfer Service
beats.text: From S3, Azure, HDFS or on-prem

beats.say: Moving MySQL to Cloud SQL with almost no downtime? Database Migration Service.
beats.label: Database to database
beats.head: Database Migration Service
beats.text: To Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, minimal downtime

beats.say: Streaming every database change into BigQuery? Datastream.
beats.label: Changes into BigQuery
beats.head: Datastream

beats.say: And BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads tables on a schedule, from apps and other warehouses.
beats.label: Scheduled loads into BigQuery
beats.head: BigQuery Data Transfer Service

beats.say: The trap: Storage Transfer Service moves files into buckets. It does not load BigQuery tables.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Storage Transfer Service moves files, not tables.

beats.say: Idea two: the plan. Five steps, always in this order.
Assess what you have. Plan the target. Migrate in waves. Validate against the source. Then optimize.
beats.label: The order

beats.say: Run old and new side by side. That is how you prove no row went missing.
beats.label: Why waves
beats.head: Run old and new side by side

beats.say: And the Hadoop cluster? Swap each part for a managed one.
Spark jobs go to Dataproc. HDFS becomes Cloud Storage. HBase becomes Bigtable.
beats.label: Hadoop to Google Cloud

beats.say: And your scheduler becomes Cloud Composer, which is managed Airflow.
beats.label: The scheduler
beats.head: Cron, Oozie → Cloud Composer

beats.say: Keep the data in Cloud Storage, not on cluster disks. Then you can delete the cluster after each job.
beats.label: Why Cloud Storage
beats.head: Data outlives the cluster

beats.say: Recap.
Do the maths first. Match the job to the tool. And follow the five steps, with validation before the switch.
beats.label: Station 1.4
items: Five steps, validate before the switch

beats.say: That is line one done. Try the checkpoint below.
